svg.title: Planned Type-directed Syn consensus and node identity
svg.desc: An exact adopted canonical Type release supplies its consensus policy. A resolver checks authority, conflict ownership, roster and disclosure. Same-custody Types use an authenticated Raft log; independent-custody Types use a BFT event DAG and Hashgraph ordering. Both feed one deterministic Syn reducer and policy-bound proof verification. All nodes are addressed by account public-key hash and all peer traffic travels through encrypted Syn pub-sub. Components are proposed.

g.text: The canonical Type decides how Syn reaches agreement.
Proposed architecture · every node is referenced by its own account public-key hash
Canonical Type release + explicit consensusPolicy
Exact definition and policy digests · governed adoption · old-policy-approved changes
An arbitrary URI, metadata field or caller-selected mode cannot establish authority.
Policy resolver and consensus router
Bind stream/epoch + node-hash roster + custody constraints + conflict ownership + disclosure group.
Unknown profile: hold. Incompatible atomic write sets: reject. No weaker-policy bypass.
Same verified custody root
Authenticated Raft-style operator log
Issuer certificate + fresh account-key possession
3 configured voters need 2 · 2 voters need both
Crash/partition model; authorised nodes trusted
First candidate: raft-rs core + Syn-owned I/O
A shared root is one correlated trust boundary.
Independent custody roots
BFT event DAG + Hashgraph virtual voting
Availability → one final order → Syn reducer
4 independent voting roots · quorum 3 · fault 1
Cap aggregate issuer weight; no child-key Sybil gain
First investigation: Hiero integration feasibility
Transport, signing, proof and key-policy gates remain.
Deterministic Syn outcome + independent policy-bound proof verification
Availability, final order and application-state evidence are distinct. Potbot admits the result locally.
A committed assignment still needs Potbot permission and independent verification of the external work.
Shared boundary: encrypted Syn-only P2P pub-sub + protected native custody
Agents hold assigned account key + current group key. Base keys stay with their operators.
Design illustration · consensus profiles and federated interoperability require implementation and acceptance evidence.
